thread:
maria: Heads up — prod-eu LB is showing a bunch of 502s and a lot of GPU-worker pods stuck in NotReady. Rolling alerts from the console. Anyone already looking?
liam: Seeing same — ALB target registration keeps failing for nodes in eu-central1. Health checks failing with connection reset.
sam: Can you paste the healthcheck logs / kube events?
maria: kube events: 
```
Warning  Unhealthy  2m (x10 over 5m)  kubelet  Readiness probe failed: dial tcp 10.x.x.x:10250: connect: connection refused
```
liam: ALB health checks use source port range ephemeral -> target port 10250. If NACL is blocking ephemeral high ports then return traffic will be dropped (stateless).
jen-oncall: I just saw a terraform apply got merged ~20m ago from infra-automation that touched network ACLs for the eu subnets. @maria can you check commit id?
maria: commit d3f2a9c applied by infra-automation — added a deny rule for tcp ports 49152-65535 because of a mistaken copy-paste from a different account.
sam: Oof. That'll break ALB <-> node TCP flows because NACLs are stateless and you need both directions allowed. The deny is outbound on the subnet, so healthcheck SYN makes it to node but response is dropped.
liam: Confirmed with tcpdump on one node: SYN from ALB arrives, node responds with SYN-ACK but we never see it leave the subnet.
jen-oncall: TL;DR — NACL deny is the culprit. What's fastest remediation?
maria: Options: 1) Revert the terraform change to restore original allow rule (safer), 2) Add explicit allow for ephemeral range on both inbound+outbound NACL entries, 3) As emergency, open a security group rule to allow ALB source IPs to target port (but SG won't fix NACL).
sam: SG won't bypass NACL. We need to update NACL. I'll push a quick terraform revert PR and plan/app. @deploy-bot please hold any infra automation applies in the region until we fix.
infra-bot: auto-merge-guard: blocking merges for infra-automation in eu subnets until manual override.
liam: While PR lands, we can temp patch with aws cli (manual) if you want to avoid waiting for CI:
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0a1b2c3d --rule-number 100 --protocol tcp --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0a1b2c3d --rule-number 100 --protocol tcp --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --ingress --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0
```
maria: I need a thumbs-up to run that manual change from oncall. It will be quick but manual changes are scary.
jen-oncall: do it, runbooks referenced. I'm monitoring.
sam: I'll watch the ALB target health after you apply.
maria: Applied manual allow entries. Monitoring...
liam: Targets are starting to register. Health checks passing on most nodes now. 502s dropping.
sam: Great. Merge the revert PR and then apply via terraform asap to make this durable.
maria: Revert PR open: #4827. I'll coordinate with infra-automation to revoke their ephemeral deny rule and add a comment explaining why ephemeral ranges can't be globally denied on shared subnets.
jen-oncall: Postmortem note: don't copy NACL configs between accounts; consider using managed modules that parameterize ephemeral rules per environment. I'll start an incident ticket.
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-124 — "NACL ephemeral deny caused ALB health failures in eu"
liam: Also add an alert to watch terraform diffs for network_acl_rule resources that modify port ranges. We should catch these in plan-review.
maria: Agreed. Thanks everyone — closing once PR is applied and terraform run completes. :thumbsup:
